title: Letta / MemGPT — where the paper and the code part ways
subtitle: Only the divergent steps are drawn. Each node states both sides; the lane says which stage of the pipeline the divergence sits in.
source: paper arXiv:2310.08560v2 (txt:/libtxt: two incompatible pdftotext extractions)  ×  repo letta @ origin/archive 56ba9c25   ·   servers/letta/verification.md, 162 assertions checked across 3 documents (128 ✓ / 6 ✗ / 28 ◐)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · paper ↔ code divergence
legend_notes: The single biggest correction (verification §7 priority #1): the architecture docs described the paper-faithful compaction path (Summarizer, 30% message-count evict) as the default. It is not — default letta_v1_agent → LettaAgentV3 uses compact_messages with a 100%/90%-of-context-window token threshold, and its summarizer model can be swapped for a cheaper one.

Structural mirror at B8: the paper's single explicit heartbeat flag becomes the code's implicit 'did you call a tool' rule — same node position, same job, opposite control signal, and neither side documents a step cap.

Two 'unreachable path' findings anchor d7: the docs' own citations (legacy sleeptime_multi_agent.py, legacy letta/agent.py:Agent) point at code with zero live callers — `git grep def load_agent` returns nothing, so the REST route that would construct the legacy agent is itself broken.
